drills.q: Name the three lines of defense and one deliverable each owns for models.
drills.a: 1st: developers/users - documentation, remediation. 2nd: MRM - independent validation, findings register, approval recommendations. 3rd: internal audit - tests that the MRM PROCESS ran as policy requires.

drills.q: PSI between development and current population = 0.32. What do you do?
drills.a: >0.25 = action band: investigate driver (macro shift vs pipeline bug), freeze promotions riding the shift, recalibrate/redevelop through change control if the shift is real and permanent, tighten compensating controls meanwhile.

drills.q: Challenger beats champion by +0.035 AUC on 800 shadow observations over 3 weeks. Promote?
drills.a: No: sample below ~1,000 minimum, no seasonal cycle covered (3 weeks), significance unproven at that n. Extend shadow period to cover a full cycle, run paired-bootstrap significance, verify guardrail metrics unchanged.

drills.q: Which Whale control failure maps to 'renegotiating limit breaches'?
drills.a: Escalation/limit governance: breaches should force de-risking or documented exceptions with authority; renegotiating them under profit pressure converted a limit system into a suggestion box - a core finding of the Senate report alongside the unvalidated VaR change.

drills.q: A Tier 3 summarizer is being repurposed to draft credit-decision memos. Governance step?
drills.a: Re-tier immediately: customer/decision impact now material -> Tier 1/2 validation before expanded use. Silent scope expansion is misuse risk; approved-use boundaries must change through change control first.

drills.q: Give three concrete signs of validator independence theater in an audit.
drills.a: Validation SLAs shorter than any genuine analysis takes; near-100% approval rates with only Low-severity findings ever issued; validators permanently embedded in delivery squads reporting to the business line they review.

drills.q: Your LLM agent hallucinated a fee amount to 40 customers last month. SR 11-7-style handling?
drills.a: Log as model-risk event with severity + root-cause class (retrieval miss vs reasoning error); check monitoring trend vs tolerance band; apply compensating controls (grounded-output constraints, human review on fee topics); feed incident into eval suite as regression case; report per policy. Hallucination = model-risk event, not just a bug ticket.

drills.q: Why does tiering exist rather than full validation for everything?
drills.a: Validation capacity is finite: GSIBs hold thousands of models, so uniform Tier 1 depth creates multi-year queues where real risk hides in backlog. Concentrate depth by materiality x complexity x novelty; accept lighter periodic review where impact is small and reversible.
